factual_problem: Mapping 'a person's judgement' to the non-physical/administrative side misleads on security guards, which ISC2 CC teaches as PHYSICAL controls (guards, dogs, lighting). A learner who generalises this hint will misfile guards. 'logic running in ... hardware' vs 'something solid' also blurs for an electronic/badge lock.
reason: The three clauses are the three bucket definitions in bucket order (Technical, Administrative, Physical), so it is close to restating the taxonomy, but it is the defining distinction and still requires the learner to decide what each control's enforcer is. No lexical echo of item text. Not a shortcut.

Pure anti-heuristic (enforcer, not asset). Slight narrowing: 'something guarding a computer may be enforced by people' nudges toward AUP / background checks being non-technical, but those items do not name a computer, so it pins nothing. The 'building enforced by software' half has no matching item here (decoy-free), so it costs nothing and teaches transfer.

factual_problem: The flip test ('what would you have broken') fails for aspirational Canon IV duties: not mentoring juniors breaks no 'standard practitioners hold each other to', so the hint steers the mentoring item away from IV or leaves it unplaceable. Canon IV is about advancing the profession, not only peer standards.
reason: Lexical anchors bypass the concept: 'deceit' matches 'exaggerate a threat ... to frighten' and 'lawbreaking' matches 'no written authorisation to test', pinning both to II by word association; 'standards practitioners hold each other to' matches 'report a peer', pinning the exam-leak item to IV. Partly redundant with bucket labels (honestly/legally), which keeps it below HIGH, but it sharpens the keyword match rather than teaching the duty-ranking-vs-subject distinction.

'before anyone can say how likely or how damaging it is' echoes 'Assess likelihood x impact', and 'a vulnerability, not yet a risk' echoes 'the vulnerabilities they could exploit'. A learner who knows nothing about risk management can place Identify at 1 and Assess at 2 purely by text matching. It pins two of five positions outright.

factual_problem: Assumes the chosen treatment is mitigation. If the treatment is accept, transfer or avoid there is no control to 'apply and verify', and transfer does not make the risk 'go down' for the asset; the hint presents a mitigation-only path as the general lifecycle.
reason: 'picked' maps to 'Choose a treatment', 'isn't working yet' maps to 'verify it actually works', and 'steps that only make sense once you can see what that achieved' maps to 'Document the residual risk'. That pins Choose < Apply < Residual (positions 3-4-5) by verb matching. Combined with hint 0, the entire sequence is given away without understanding.

factual_problem: Guidelines do not sit in a 'chain where each carries out the one above'; they are non-binding advisory material alongside standards/procedures. Forcing every internal item into the chain invites placing the passphrase guideline as a link (e.g. as a standard or procedure). The chain also omits that policies are themselves driven by laws/regulations (ISC2 CC presents regulations at the top of the hierarchy).
reason: Method only: relational placement, no item-specific wording or keyword echo. The learner still has to know what each layer implements. 'internal documents' quietly separates HIPAA as external, a mild narrowing of one item, but that item is trivially identifiable anyway.
